identity.title: The ALMA-ATOMS-QUARKS Survey: Resolving a Chemically Rich Massive Protostellar Outflow

paper_type_evidence.quote: We present a comprehensive study on the physical and chemical structures of a chemically rich bipolar outflow in a high-mass star forming region IRAS 16272−4837 (SDC335), utilizing high-resolution spectral line data at 1.3 mm and 3 mm dual-bands from the ALMA ATOMS and QUARKS surveys.

evidence.quote: To overcome these limitations, we resolve a chemically rich massive protostellar outflow in the high-mass star-forming region IRDC SDC335.579−0.292 (IRAS 16272−4837, also G335.59-0.29, hereafter SDC335), which is located at a distance of 3.54 kpc.

question.value: What are the physical and chemical structures and the chemical origins of molecular species within the bipolar protostellar outflow of the high-mass star-forming region SDC335?

evidence.quote: We present a comprehensive study on the physical and chemical structures of a chemically rich bipolar outflow in a high-mass star forming region IRAS 16272−4837 (SDC335), utilizing high-resolution spectral line data at 1.3 mm and 3 mm dual-bands from the ALMA ATOMS and QUARKS surveys.
In Section 4, we further explore the chemical origin of each species within these local regions.

We utilized ALMA Band 3 data from the ATOMS survey (Project ID: 2019.1.00685.S; PI: Tie Liu; T. Liu et al. 2020), which targets 146 massive star-forming clumps using both the 12-m array in C3 configuration and the ACA 7-m array.

findings_qualitative.value: Emission from CO, SiO, SO, H2CO, and CH3OH separates morphologically into a high-velocity (>12 km s^-1) collimated jet along the outflow axis and a low-velocity (6-12 km s^-1) hollow-shell cavity structure.

evidence.loc: 3.2. Molecular lines detected along the outflow
evidence.quote: The resulting channel maps reveal that emission from CO 2–1, SiO 5–4, SO 6 5–5 4, H2CO 3 0,3–2 0,2, and CH3OH 4 −2,3–3 −1,2 is morphologically separated into two kinematic components: a high-velocity (> 12 km s−1) component concentrated along the collimated outflow axis, and a low-velocity (6–12 km s−1) component forming a hollow-shell cavity structure.

findings_qualitative.value: Molecular species in the SDC335 outflow are regulated by three main mechanisms: (1) direct entrainment from the natal core (CO, 13CO, HCO+, H2CO, CS, HC3N), (2) shock-induced grain sputtering and high-temperature shock chemistry (SiO, SO, HCN, H13CN, DCN, HC3N), and (3) thermal desorption and gas-phase chemistry driven by shock heating (CH3OH, HNCO, CH3CHO, CH3CN, CH3OCHO).

evidence.quote: By analyzing the spatial distribution and kinematics of these molecular lines, we find that the molecular inventory in the outflow is regulated by three processes: (i) direct entrainment from the natal molecular core by the outflow; (ii) shock-induced release of molecules or atoms from dust grains; and (iii) thermal desorption and gas-phase reactions driven by shock heating.

claims.hypothesis: The rich molecular inventory along the massive protostellar outflow in SDC335 originates from multiple distinct physical and chemical mechanisms rather than a single pathway.
claims.experiment: Extracted spectra, channel maps, PVDs, and integrated intensity ratios relative to 13CO for 35 transitions of 22 species from ALMA Band 3 (ATOMS) and Band 6 (QUARKS) data, and performed PCA and Kendall rank correlation analysis.
claims.result: PCA separates the molecular PVDs into distinct quadrants (PC1 and PC2 explain 46.5% of variance): entrained species (CO, 13CO, HCO+, H2CO, CS, HC3N), shock-sputtered/formed species (SiO, SO, HCN, H13CN, DCN), and shock-heated thermally desorbed COMs (CH3OH, HNCO, CH3CHO, CH3CN, CH3OCHO).
claims.finding: Outflow chemistry in SDC335 has a multi-origin nature regulated jointly by direct core entrainment, shock-induced grain sputtering, and thermal desorption/gas-phase reactions from shock heating.

evidence.quote: By analyzing the spatial distribution and kinematics of these molecular lines, we find that the molecular inventory in the outflow is regulated by three processes: (i) direct entrainment from the natal molecular core by the outflow; (ii) shock-induced release of molecules or atoms from dust grains; and (iii) thermal desorption and gas-phase reactions driven by shock heating.
The observed chemistry of the outflow is therefore shaped by the interplay of all three mechanisms rather than by a single pathway.

claims.hypothesis: Enhancements of COMs and species such as CH3OH, HNCO, and CH3CHO at outflow knots are driven by localized shock heating and thermal desorption rather than direct high-velocity grain sputtering.
claims.experiment: Analyzed line profiles and PVDs of COMs along the outflow and compared the spatial derivative of the SiO/13CO intensity ratio with H2CO rotational temperatures derived via RADEX.
claims.result: COMs peak near the systemic velocity with narrow profiles, and bright knots exhibit elevated H2CO rotational temperatures (T_rot >= 200 K) that correlate with steep SiO/13CO spatial gradients (r = 0.36).
claims.finding: Elevated abundances of CH3OH, HNCO, and COMs at the knots are primarily driven by local thermal heating in shocked gas that sublimates icy mantles and drives high-temperature gas-phase chemistry.

evidence.quote: Independent constraints from H2CO rotational analysis (Fig. B4) reveal Trot ≳ 200 K at several knots, consistent with strong shock heating by the protostellar jet
In summary, the elevated abundances of CH 3 OH, HNCO, and several COMs are mainly attributed to high temperatures induced by jet–ambient shocks.

fixed.old: The PCA distribution naturally separates molecules into three quadrants, corresponding to three predominant classes: (1) species entrained from the dense core by the outflow (e.g., CO, HCO+, CS, HC3N); (2) molecules released into the gas phase or newly formed in jet-induced shocks (e.g., SiO, SO, HCN, DCN); and (3) molecules thermally excited by shock heating and subsequent gas-phase or desorption processes (e.g., CH3OH, CH3CHO, CH3CN, HNCO, CH3OCHO).
fixed.new: regulated by three processes: (i) direct entrainment from the natal molecular core by the outflow; (ii) shock-induced release of molecules or atoms from dust grains; and (iii) thermal desorption and gas-phase reactions driven by shock heating.
